questions.q: Match each renal level with its vertebral correspondence — 1) Fetal kidney position 2) Adult kidney position 3) Renal hilum … A) T12–L3 B) S1–S3 C) L1
questions.exp: The fetal kidneys sit at S1–S3 and ascend with rotation to the adult T12–L3 position; the hilum corresponds to L1. (Book p711)

questions.q: Fill up: The fetal kidneys at S1–S3 ascend to the adult T12–L3 position accompanied by ______.
questions.exp: The book's arrow reads 'ascend with rotation' from the fetal S1–S3 level to the adult T12–L3 level. (Book p711)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about renal vertebral levels is TRUE?
opts: The renal hilum corresponds to the L1 vertebral level
The fetal kidneys lie at T12–L3
The hilum corresponds to the L3 vertebral level
questions.exp: Hilum = L1; the fetal (not adult) kidneys are at S1–S3 and the adult (not fetal) kidneys span T12–L3. (Book p711)

questions.q: The left kidney sits at a higher vertebral level than the right because of:
opts: The liver occupying the right upper quadrant
The spleen pushing the left kidney upward
The left adrenal gland being larger
The aorta lying to the left of midline
questions.exp: Left kidney is higher due to the liver on the right side pushing the right kidney down. (Book p711)

questions.q: The renal artery arises as which numbered lateral branch of the abdominal aorta in the book's ordered list?
questions.exp: Lateral branches of the abdominal aorta in order: 1st inferior phrenic, 2nd middle suprarenal, 3rd renal, 4th gonadal artery. (Book p711)

questions.q: Match each position in the lateral-branch sequence of the abdominal aorta with its artery — 1) First 2) Second 3) Third 4) Fourth … A) Middle suprarenal artery B) Inferior phrenic artery C) Gonadal artery D) Renal artery
questions.exp: Sequence: 1st inferior phrenic, 2nd middle suprarenal, 3rd renal, 4th gonadal artery. (Book p711)

questions.q: Fill up: Between the two renal arteries, the ______ renal artery is the longer one.
questions.exp: The right renal artery is longer (it crosses behind the IVC to reach the right kidney). (Book p711)

questions.q: Both the right and the left renal vein drain into the:
questions.exp: Right and left renal veins both drain into the IVC. (Book p711)

questions.q: All of the following describe the left renal vein EXCEPT:
opts: It is shorter than the right renal vein
It is longer than the right renal vein
It is compressed by a superior mesenteric artery aneurysm
questions.exp: The left renal vein is longer, crosses the midline and can be compressed by an SMA aneurysm; it is not shorter than the right. (Book p711)

questions.q: Fill up: The ureteric and gonadal veins join the adrenal vein to drain into the ______.
questions.exp: Tributaries of the left renal vein: ureteral vein, gonadal vein and adrenal vein. (Book p711)

questions.q: A 58-year-old is found to have a superior mesenteric artery aneurysm on angiography. Which vessel does the book say such an aneurysm compresses?
questions.exp: Superior mesenteric artery aneurysm compresses the left renal vein. (Book p711)

questions.q: In the gross-anatomy-of-kidney figure, which two structures are shown as cut?
questions.exp: The figure labels 'Esophagus (cut)' and 'Rectum (cut)' among the posterior-abdominal-wall structures. (Book p711)

questions.q: Before living donation, a Tc-99 DTPA scan is used to measure single-kidney GFR; the book states that the kidney retained with the donor is the one with:
questions.exp: Tc-99 DTPA gives single-kidney GFR and the higher-GFR kidney is retained with the donor. (Book p711)

questions.q: Fill up: In the transplant anastomosis table, the donor ureter is joined to the recipient's ______.
questions.exp: Donor ureter is anastomosed to the recipient bladder. (Book p711)

questions.q: Match each donor structure with its recipient anastomotic partner — 1) Ureter 2) Renal artery 3) Renal vein … A) External iliac vein B) Bladder C) Internal iliac artery (preferred over external iliac artery and aorta)
questions.exp: Ureter→bladder; renal artery→internal iliac artery (over external iliac artery/aorta); renal vein→external iliac vein. (Book p711)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the transplant arterial anastomosis is TRUE?
opts: The internal iliac artery is preferred over the external iliac artery and aorta
The external iliac artery is preferred over the internal iliac artery
The aorta is the first-choice recipient vessel
The renal artery is anastomosed to the external iliac vein
questions.exp: The table lists internal iliac artery > external iliac artery, aorta for the donor renal artery; the renal vein goes to the external iliac vein. (Book p711)

questions.q: The donor kidney is placed in the recipient's:
questions.exp: Donor kidney goes into the right iliac fossa; the recipient's own kidneys are retained in the same place. (Book p711)

questions.q: All of the following are true of renal transplantation EXCEPT:
opts: The recipient's native kidneys are removed during the operation
The donor kidney lies in the right iliac fossa
The recipient's own kidneys are retained in the same place
The donor ureter is anastomosed to the bladder
questions.exp: Recipient kidneys are retained in the same place (not removed); donor kidney sits in the right iliac fossa and its ureter joins the bladder. (Book p711)

questions.q: All of the following are posterior relations of the kidney EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Posterior relations per the figure: diaphragmatic area, area for transversalis tendon, area for quadratus lumborum and area for psoas (with 11th/12th ribs and L1–L2 transverse processes); the ascending colon is an anterior relation. (Book p712)

questions.q: Fill up: Posteriorly, the kidney rests against the eleventh and the ______ ribs.
questions.exp: The posterior-relations figure labels the eleventh and twelfth ribs over the upper poles. (Book p712)

questions.q: The transverse processes of which two vertebrae are shown as posterior relations of the kidneys?
questions.exp: The figure labels transverse processes of the first lumbar vertebra and of the second lumbar vertebra. (Book p712)

questions.q: Match each operation with its surgical approach — 1) Laparoscopic retroperitoneal adrenalectomy 2) Nephrectomy … A) Anterior approach in the supine position B) Posterior approach
questions.exp: Laparoscopic retroperitoneal adrenalectomy uses the posterior approach; nephrectomy uses the anterior approach in supine position. (Book p712)

questions.q: The number of minor calyces per kidney given in the book is:
questions.exp: Calyces: major 3–4, minor 9–12. (Book p712)

questions.q: Fill up: The apex of a renal pyramid protrudes into a ______ calyx.
questions.exp: Pyramid: base at the corticomedullary junction, apex protruding into a minor calyx, tip = papilla. (Book p712)

questions.q: The vital structure at the tip of a renal pyramid is the:
questions.exp: Tip of the pyramid = papilla, labelled a vital structure. (Book p712)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the renal pyramid is TRUE?
opts: Its base lies at the corticomedullary junction
Its apex faces the renal capsule
Its base opens into the major calyx
Its tip is avascular and non-vital
questions.exp: Base = corticomedullary junction; apex protrudes into the minor calyx and the tip (papilla) is vital. (Book p712)

questions.q: The renal columns of Bertini are:
opts: Cortical tissue extending between the bases of the pyramids
Medullary tracts running within the pyramids
Fibrous septa of the renal capsule
Vascular bundles of the renal sinus
questions.exp: Renal columns of Bertini = cortical tissue extending between the base of the pyramids. (Book p712)

questions.q: The renal medulla is prone to hypoxia because it has:
opts: Lesser blood supply with slow, sluggish flow
A richer capillary network than the cortex
Direct arterial inflow from the gonadal artery
questions.exp: Medulla has lesser blood supply (slow flow, sluggish) and is therefore prone to hypoxia. (Book p712)

questions.q: A diabetic patient passes tissue fragments in the urine; the book's sequence for this event is that the papilla detaches easily, is excreted with urine, and culminates in:
questions.exp: Papilla is the most vulnerable part of the medulla; it detaches easily, is excreted with urine and produces papillary necrosis. (Book p712)

questions.q: All of the following are labelled in the 'Parts of Kidney' figure EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The figure labels interlobular/arcuate/interlobar/lobar/segmental arteries and veins, renal column, papilla, cortex, minor and major calyx, medullary pyramid, renal capsule, renal pelvis and ureter — but no glomerulus. (Book p712)

questions.q: In the intrarenal arterial sequence of the figure, the artery lying between the lobar and the arcuate arteries is the:
questions.exp: Figure order: segmental → lobar → interlobar → arcuate → interlobular arteries. (Book p712)

questions.q: The book defines an uncomplicated urinary tract infection as cystitis occurring in a:
opts: Sexually active, young adult, healthy female
questions.exp: Uncomplicated UTI = cystitis in a sexually active, young adult, healthy female; everything else falls under complicated. (Book p713)

questions.q: All of the following are features of uncomplicated cystitis EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Uncomplicated cystitis: urgency, frequency, dysuria, no h/o fever and no flank pain. (Book p713)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about uncomplicated cystitis is TRUE?
opts: There is no history of fever
Flank pain is a defining feature
It is synonymous with complicated UTI
questions.exp: Uncomplicated cystitis has no history of fever and no flank pain; it is the opposite arm of complicated UTI. (Book p713)

questions.q: The drug of choice for uncomplicated urinary tract infection is:
questions.exp: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BD × 3–5 days is the DOC; cotrimoxazole 200 mg BD × 3–5 days and fosfomycin 3 g sachet are the listed alternatives. (Book p713)

questions.q: The single-dose sachet regimen of fosfomycin for uncomplicated UTI is:
questions.exp: Fosfomycin 3 g, 1 sachet, is one of the uncomplicated-UTI regimens. (Book p713)

questions.q: Match each uncomplicated-UTI drug with its book dose — 1) Nitrofurantoin 2) Cotrimoxazole 3) Fosfomycin … A) 3 g, one sachet B) 100 mg BD × 3–5 days C) 200 mg BD × 3–5 days
questions.exp: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BD × 3–5 days (DOC); cotrimoxazole 200 mg BD × 3–5 days; fosfomycin 3 g one sachet. (Book p713)

questions.q: In the UTI flowchart, the 'complicated' arm is defined as:
questions.exp: The flowchart splits UTI into complicated ('all other causes') and uncomplicated (cystitis in the sexually active young healthy female). (Book p713)

questions.q: In the UTI investigation protocol, ultrasound is used to rule out all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: USG rules out obstruction, emphysematous pyelonephritis and pelvicalyceal anatomical abnormalities; renal artery stenosis is not on that list. (Book p713)

questions.q: After a normal ultrasound the diagnosis is acute pyelonephritis; the book's injectable treatment options include amikacin and:
questions.exp: Rx for acute pyelonephritis: amikacin (S/E nephrotoxicity) plus beta-lactam inhibitors such as cefoperazone-sulbactam or piperacillin-tazobactam. (Book p713)

questions.q: Fill up: Among the acute pyelonephritis drugs, the one flagged in the book for nephrotoxicity as a side effect is ______.
questions.exp: Amikacin is listed with the side effect nephrotoxicity. (Book p713)

questions.q: In renal failure, the book adjusts piperacillin + tazobactam from 4.5 g IV QID to:
questions.exp: Piperacillin + tazobactam 4.5 g IV QID normally, reduced to 4.5 g IV BD in renal failure. (Book p713)

questions.q: Fill up: When the patient is not responding, CECT abdomen is done using low-volume, ______ contrast.
questions.exp: Step 2 of the protocol is CECT abdomen with low-volume, iso-osmolar contrast. (Book p713)

questions.q: All of the following are CECT features of acute pyelonephritis EXCEPT:
questions.exp: CECT of acute pyelonephritis shows a slightly enlarged kidney, thickened infundibulum and ureter, and patchy hypodensities — not a contracted kidney. (Book p714)

questions.q: Papillary necrosis is defined as detachment of the papilla from:
questions.exp: Papillary necrosis = detachment of the papilla from the tip of the pyramid. (Book p714)

questions.q: All of the following are listed causes of papillary necrosis EXCEPT:
opts: Uncomplicated cystitis in a healthy female
Complicated UTI in a diabetic patient
questions.exp: Causes: complicated UTI in diabetics, analgesic nephropathy, snake bite and sickle cell anemia; uncomplicated cystitis is not a cause. (Book p714)

questions.q: Fill up: Analgesic nephropathy follows phenacetin + aspirin + ______ and progresses to CKD.
questions.exp: Analgesic nephropathy = phenacetin + aspirin + caffeine leading to CKD. (Book p714)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about papillary necrosis is TRUE?
opts: Its prognosis is excellent with observation alone
It spares the tip of the pyramid
questions.exp: Prognosis of papillary necrosis is poor; it involves the papilla at the pyramid tip and follows analgesics among other causes. (Book p714)

questions.q: Match each papillary-necrosis stage label with its appearance — 1) Stage C 2) Stage E 3) Stage G … A) Lobster claw appearance B) Calyceal blunting C) Ball on tree appearance
questions.exp: In the types diagram C = ball on tree appearance, E = lobster claw appearance and G = calyceal blunting. (Book p715)

questions.q: In the types-of-papillary-necrosis diagram, all of the following are TRUE EXCEPT:
opts: Stages B and C form the medullary type
Stages D, E and F form the papillary type
questions.exp: Stage A is the normal calyx and papilla; B–C are the medullary type, D–F the papillary type and G calyceal blunting. (Book p715)

questions.q: Renal abscess is described in the book as a complication of UTI with a prognosis that is:
questions.exp: Renal abscess: a complication of UTI with poor prognosis. (Book p715)

questions.q: In the childhood UTI protocol, a complicated UTI is treated for how long before the first ultrasound?
questions.exp: Childhood protocol: complicated UTI → Rx for 2 weeks → then USG. (Book p715)

questions.q: CAKUT stands for congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract; the book's examples are:
opts: Medullary sponge kidney and simple cysts
questions.exp: CAKUT examples given: double pelvis and duplicated ureter. (Book p715)

questions.q: If CAKUT is positive on ultrasound, the next investigation in the childhood UTI protocol is:
questions.exp: CAKUT (+) → step 2 VCU/MCU to look for VUR and posterior urethral valve; DMSA comes only after VUR (+). (Book p715)

questions.q: Fill up: On VCU/MCU the protocol looks for vesicoureteric reflux and, in males, the posterior urethral ______.
questions.exp: VCU/MCU looks for vesicoureteric reflux (VUR) and posterior urethral valve in males. (Book p715)

questions.q: Once VUR is confirmed, the DMSA scan in the childhood protocol is used to assess:
questions.exp: Step 3 DMSA scan assesses the degree of scarring once VUR is positive. (Book p715)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about renal nuclear scans is TRUE?
opts: The DTPA scan gives the GFR of the two kidneys separately
The DMSA scan gives the GFR of the two kidneys separately
The DTPA scan assesses the degree of scarring
The DMSA scan is used to grade VUR
questions.exp: Note: DTPA scan = GFR of kidneys separately; DMSA scan = degree of scarring. (Book p715)

questions.q: A 6-year-old with reflux nephropathy needs the separate function of each kidney measured before surgery. The scan the book recommends for kidney-wise GFR is:
questions.exp: DTPA scan gives the GFR of the kidneys separately, so it is the study for split function. (Book p715)

questions.q: The VUR figure on the last page of the chapter displays which grading range alongside a normal study?
questions.exp: The figure panels are labelled Grade-1, Grade-2, Grade-3, Grade-4, Grade-5 and Normal. (Book p716)

questions.q: Asymmetric involvement of the kidneys is attributed in the book to VUR and to:
questions.exp: Note: asymmetric involvement of kidneys — VUR and renal artery disease. (Book p716)

questions.q: Match each papillary type with its features — 1) Composite papillae 2) Simple conical papillae … A) Mid pole (66%), slit-like closed orifices, cone shaped, do not allow reflux B) Upper and lower pole (33%), flat/concave surface with round/oval opening, open gaping orifices, allow reflux
questions.exp: Composite papillae (upper/lower pole 33%, flat-concave surface, open gaping orifices) allow reflux; simple conical papillae (mid pole 66%, slit-like closed orifices) do not. (Book p716)

questions.q: The proportion of children having at least one compound papilla is:
questions.exp: 90% of children have at least one compound papilla. (Book p716)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about papillary types is TRUE?
opts: Composite papillae allow reflux whereas simple conical papillae do not
Simple conical papillae allow reflux whereas composite papillae do not
Both papillary types allow reflux equally
questions.exp: Composite papillae have open gaping orifices and allow reflux; simple conical papillae have closed slit-like orifices and don't. (Book p716)

questions.q: Fill up: The channels opening onto the papillary surface in the papillae diagram are the ducts of ______.
questions.exp: The diagram labels the ducts of Bellini opening on the papillary surface. (Book p716)

questions.q: Composite papillae are most frequent at which poles, in which order?
opts: Upper and lower pole, upper more than lower
Upper and lower pole, lower more than upper
questions.exp: Composite papillae occur at the upper and lower pole (33%), upper > lower. (Book p716)

questions.q: Simple conical papillae are located at the mid pole in what percentage?
questions.exp: Simple conical papillae sit at the mid pole (66%). (Book p716)
